According to the Hong Kong Observatory, minimum temperatures will fall to 21 degrees on Wednesday and drop noticeably to 15 degrees on Friday and 16 degrees on Saturday. “A cold front has formed over the northern part of southern China and will move across the coast of Guangdong later [on Wednesday]. Locally, there will...

Xi, who was meeting the Canadian leader for the second time this year, called for greater “political trust through...

item.author: Chris Tsang
item.dc:creator: Chris Tsang
item.description: Hong Kong’s property market is expected to weather a return to higher interest rates better than during the previous tightening cycle, with analysts saying stronger housing fundamentals should help cushion the impact. Such a shift would be “more bearable” than during the 2022-23 round of rate increases, S&P Global Ratings said in a report published on Tuesday. “The Hong Kong residential market is in better shape to absorb them,” it added. “Demand-supply dynamics have improved over the past two...
item.title: Hong Kong property market can absorb rate increases better than before: analysts

item.dc:creator: Eric Jiang,Lexi Tian
item.description: A Hong Kong private hospital has apologised for a medical blunder in which a woman’s ovaries were wrongly removed in a surgery that was meant to take out only her uterus and fallopian tubes. The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) Medical Centre apologised on Tuesday, a day after the Department of Health disclosed the incident in its monthly list of sentinel events in private hospitals. Without naming the hospital, the department stated earlier that a 45-year-old female patient had both of...

item.author: Carol Yang
item.dc:creator: Carol Yang
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping has pledged to deepen connectivity between China and Vietnam and better integrate their shared interests in a meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart To Lam. President Lam arrived in Shenzhen earlier on Tuesday for the Apec summit. Vietnam will host next year’s gathering. item.title: China and Vietnam should ‘weather the storm together’, Xi tells Lam in Shenzhen

item.author: Alice Yan
item.dc:creator: Alice Yan
item.description: A noodle chain in eastern China that offers free meals to anyone, without setting any eligibility criteria, has found itself at the centre of controversy after nearby eateries complained of a sharp drop in customers. The brand, “Zero Yuan Noodle Restaurant,” has two outlets in Nanjing, Jiangsu province. One is in Jiangning district, while the other is in Yuhuatai district, the Beijing News reported. Since the outlets opened in October, many people have queued outside to receive a bowl of noodles...

item.author: Resty Woro Yuniar
item.dc:creator: Resty Woro Yuniar
item.description: Conservationists and indigenous communities in Indonesia have pushed back against a government proposal to relocate critically endangered Javan rhinos to a second national park, warning a rushed transfer could threaten the species’ survival and leave their current home vulnerable to extractive industries. The debate follows remarks by Hashim Djojohadikusumo, President Prabowo Subianto’s brother and special envoy for climate and energy, who said Jakarta was considering moving some Javan rhinos...

item.author: Alcott Wei
item.dc:creator: Alcott Wei
item.description: China has charged a former senior nuclear industry executive with bribery, marking the latest downfall in its sweeping anti-corruption crackdown targeting the military and defence sectors. Gu Jun, former general manager of state-owned giant China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC), will stand trial for accepting illegal payments, the Supreme People’s Procuratorate in Beijing announced on Tuesday. Gu is accused of long abusing his position in the nuclear power sector to secure favours for...

item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Pope Leo on Tuesday voiced hope for “less war” and “less division” following the midterm elections in his native United States, as he returned from a tour of South America. The first American pope has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump over the war with Iran and made history this month by announcing that he had cast a ballot in the midterms – the first time a pope has been known to have voted. “I would like to see a greater capacity for dialogue, for building bridges, for...
item.title: Pope Leo urges ‘less war, less division’ after US midterm elections

item.author: Biman Mukherji
item.dc:creator: Biman Mukherji
item.description: Pakistan’s planned purchase of 100,000 Turkish attack drones has raised concerns in India about drone swarms in any future conflict, as Islamabad deepens ties with Turkey and Saudi Arabia, its partners in the Mecca Defence Alliance. Under the three-year agreement, Pakistan will acquire Merkut drones from Turkish defence company Pasifik Teknoloji. Analysts say the deal highlights the growing importance armed forces place on drones deploying them in large numbers. The package also includes 10...

item.author: Cannix Yau,Lo Hoi-ying
item.dc:creator: Cannix Yau,Lo Hoi-ying
item.description: Hong Kong’s unemployment rate dipped to 3.8 per cent in the three months from August to October after increasing for the past two months, with more distinct drops in the food and beverage sector. Preliminary data released by the Census and Statistics Department showed the jobless rate was down 0.1 percentage points from the July-to-September period. The underemployment rate remained unchanged at 2.0 per cent. Total employment dropped by 1,200 to 3.654 million, from 3.655 million in July to...

item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: Police have thwarted an alleged mass shooting plot involving three teenagers at a school in the northern Philippines after a tip-off from the FBI, as authorities urged parents to monitor their children’s online activities. item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Authorities in Japan’s Maebashi city ordered school closures as officials were looking for a bear on the loose on Tuesday, after media reports said at least one person had been attacked. Officials in the city north of Tokyo have captured a cub, one of two animals seen roaming in residential areas. The search for the bear believed to be its mother continues. Bear sightings nationwide have sharply decreased from the last financial year, when a record 13 people were killed. Still, experts say...

The meeting, alongside the Apec summit in Shenzhen, will start at 2.30pm following a 12.45pm Trump-Xi discussion, according to the White House. item.dc:creator: Danny Mok
item.description: Two people were taken to hospital and about 200 residents fled to safety after a fire broke out in a flat at a public housing estate in Hong Kong’s Lam Tin on Tuesday. A man and a woman escaped from the flat in Kai Wong House at Kai Tin Estate on their own. The man suffered minor arm injuries and smoke inhalation, while the woman complained of discomfort after inhaling smoke. item.dc:creator: The Star

The girl, who was with some family members searching for frogs and catching fish along a river at Kampung Tinanom around 10pm on Saturday, sustained about 13 pellet wounds on multiple areas of her body from a firearm believed to be an illegal home-made shotgun known locally as a bakakuk. item.dc:creator: Albee Zhang
item.description: The first two American F-15EX Eagle II fighter jets arrived at Kadena in Okinawa, Japan on Sunday marking an upgrade for the ageing US fleet, but analysts say a shift in the regional air power balance is unlikely given China’s growing capabilities. Kadena is the first airbase to receive the F-15EX outside the United States, according to a US Air Force statement on Saturday. The new aircraft will be operated by the 44th and 67th Fighter Squadrons under the 18th Wing. They are the first of 36...

item.author: Sam Beltran
item.dc:creator: Sam Beltran
item.description: Soaring prices and a slowing economy have raised fears of stagflation in the Philippines, squeezing households and leaving the government with less policy space to reverse the trend. The country’s economy grew just 2.1 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, its weakest pace since the pandemic. Inflation surged to 7.8 per cent in October and unemployment hit 5.4 per cent in September.
